questions.q: What is a 'function' in Propp's sense?
choices: An act of a character, defined by its significance for the course of the action
A recurring image that gathers meaning
A scene that turns a value
questions.explain: Propp defines tales by what acts do in the action, not by who performs them.

questions.q: In one tale a king gives the hero an eagle; in another an old man gives him a horse. What would Propp say?
choices: They're different tales with nothing in common
They're the same function: the hero receives a magical means of reaching his goal
questions.explain: The names and objects change; the function stays the same.

questions.q: Which of Propp's claims about the wonder tales is most surprising?
choices: That every tale contains all 31 functions
That tales are best sorted by subject
That the functions that do appear always come in the same order
questions.explain: Not every tale has every function, but the sequence of those present is constant.

questions.q: A stranger tests the hero's kindness and, when he passes, gives him a magic sword. Which role is the stranger playing?
questions.explain: The donor tests the hero and supplies a magical agent. Threshold guardian is Vogler's term.

questions.q: Late in a tale, someone claims credit for the hero's deed and is later exposed. Which of Propp's roles is this?
questions.explain: The false hero makes unfounded claims and is exposed when the true hero is recognized.

questions.q: What did Propp study to reach his conclusions?
choices: Myths of heroes from around the world
One hundred Russian wonder tales from Afanasyev's collection
questions.explain: His corpus was deliberately narrow: Russian fairy tales. World myths were Campbell's territory.

questions.q: What was Lévi-Strauss's main objection to Propp?
choices: That he included too few functions
That he separated form from content and ignored what the tales mean
questions.explain: Lévi-Strauss admired the work but argued structure can't be cut off from meaning and culture.

ideas: Classify tales by what characters do for the action, not by who they are or what the tales are about.
In the wonder tale, the acts that appear always come in the same fixed order.
A tale's cast reduces to seven spheres of action, and one person can fill several of them.
A villainy or a lack sets each move of the tale in motion, and its liquidation closes it.
